mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS) reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 3-month change in FEDFUNDS is negative in more than 40% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% (as of the latest available data), it signals an active monetary tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% occurs in more than 30% of instances, but the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (3-month change > 0.1pp) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 200) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 200
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1pp in 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 200) occurs in more than 25% of instances, but the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), the market anticipates monetary policy easing, which reduces equity discount rates and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% occurs in more than 30% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts rate (measured as the 3-month change in HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which supports positive equity valuations and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 3-month change in HOUST is positive in more than 40% of instances, but the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 2000 thousand units (HOUST < 2000), it signals a weakening housing market and economic slowdown, which generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 2000 occurs in more than 30% of instances, but the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 2100) combined with a decline in residential fixed investment (RSAFS < 360000 million dollars) signals a broad-based housing market contraction, which generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST < 2100 and RSAFS < 360000) occurs in more than 25% of instances, but the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low industrial production growth regimes (INDPRO 3-month growth rate < 0.5%), the economy is slowing, which increases the risk of recession and generates negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The INDPRO 3-month growth rate < 0.5% occurs in more than 30% of instances, but the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
